subject: Collaboration inquiry from a GM2 AB variant patient group
body:
Dear NTSAD team,

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group for GM2-gangliosidosis, AB variant. I'm reaching out to introduce our community and explore whether there might be room to connect.

A paper reports that NTSAD "leads the worldwide fight to treat and cure Tay-Sachs, Canavan, GM1, and Sandhoff diseases by driving research, forging collaboration, and fostering community" [Ed912a71]. A paper also reports that NTSAD runs PRONTO – Azafaros, described as "a natural history study of GM1 and GM2 (Sandhoff and Tay-Sachs)" [E48e5738].

GM2 AB variant and Tay-Sachs share a common mechanism: a paper reports that GM2 AB variant is marked by "excessive neuronal accumulation of GM2 and related glycolipids" [E7d4ef12], and a paper reports that Tay-Sachs involves "GM2 ganglioside accumulation predominantly in lysosomes of nerve cells" [Ee7edb35]. Given this overlap, I believe our communities may have shared interests in research and natural history efforts.

Would you be open to a short introductory call to see if there's potential for collaboration or information-sharing between our groups?

Thank you for your time and for the work you do.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient Group Leader, GM2 AB Variant Community

Sources:
[Ed912a71] https://ntsad.org/diseases/sandhoff-disease/
[E48e5738] https://ntsad.org/ntsad-research/research-for-families-and-individuals/natural-history-studies/
[E7d4ef12] https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8900233/
[Ee7edb35] https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30524313/
